do_not_block_analysis.verbose_section_patterns_found: none (no Philosophy / Overview / Quality Standards / Safety Features / Helper Scripts / verbose Usage)
do_not_block_analysis.redundant_boilerplate: none — the 6 bullets each name a distinct matcher surface from spec §5.13C; no two bullets cover the same enforcement axis. Removing any bullet would leave a defense-in-depth gap that the prompt block exists to mirror.
do_not_block_analysis.concision_assessment: Optimal. Each line carries load-bearing information: matcher surface (bullets 1-6), allowlist + exit code (sentence), routing alternatives (3 bullets), citation. No expandable narrative.
do_not_block_analysis.duplication_across_7_files: Intentional and correct. The block is identical across the 7 banned agents because the harness contract IS identical for all 7. Per-agent customization would create drift and weaken the rule. This is the same pattern as the pre-existing identical 'WRITE TOOL ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN' block in those files.

summary.verdict: CLEAN — the 19-line DO-NOT block introduced in this diff across 7 banned-agent prompts is rule-mode, defense-in-depth, and load-bearing. Each line carries either a matcher-surface contract, an allowlist+exit-code contract, a positive routing alternative, or a spec citation. No story-mode 'why this matters' narrative, no Philosophy/Overview/Quality Standards verbosity, no redundant boilerplate. Block size (19 lines × 7 files = 133 lines) is justified by the 6-surface defense-in-depth contract from spec §5.13C — narrowing the block would weaken the prompt-layer mirror of the harness contract.
